title: The Man With Eighty Pack-Years — Clubbing, Crackles, and a Lifetime of Toddy, Alcohol, and Beedis

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 61 years old, presenting with grade 2 breathlessness and cough with expectoration for a week. He had been apparently well until a week before this, when he developed fever, cold symptoms, cough, and breathlessness, for which he was taken to a local hospital and given symptomatic treatment. His fever was intermittent and low-grade, improving with medication, and lasted five days. His cough produces a small amount of white, non-foul-smelling, non-bloody sputum. He denies chest pain, palpitations, orthopnea, or paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, and has no known coronary artery disease, tuberculosis, or thyroid disease.

He has used toddy since age 25 (one bottle a day) and alcohol since age 30 (90 ml a day), and has smoked two packets of beedis a day since age 50.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- **General exam:** conscious, coherent, cooperative; grade 4 clubbing present; no pallor, icterus, cyanosis, lymphadenopathy, or pedal edema
- **Vitals:** temperature 98.4°F, pulse 60 bpm regular, respiratory rate 16/min, blood pressure 110/90 mmHg
- **Head-to-toe exam:** temporal wasting; tobacco staining on the teeth; leukoplakia on the soft palate; Mallampati class 1 airway
- **Respiratory exam:** flat alar chest and pectus excavatum, with reduced chest movement and expansion on the right side (1.25 cm total), dullness to percussion in the right suprascapular area, and mid-inspiratory coarse crackles throughout the lungs, more pronounced on the left
- **Liver function:** total bilirubin 0.64 mg/dL, direct bilirubin 0.2 mg/dL, AST 20 IU/L, ALT 12 IU/L, ALP 125 IU/L, total protein 6.5 g/dL, albumin 3.6 g/dL

**Working diagnosis:** bronchiectasis, with a query of underlying pulmonary fibrosis, in the setting of decades of heavy smoking, toddy, and alcohol use.

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He had no fresh complaints on the second day, with decreased air entry and reduced chest expansion persisting on the right side; sputum was sent for AFB smear and CBNAAT testing, and he was started on nebulized ipratropium and a multivitamin. By the third day his breathlessness had resolved, and he continued on nebulized bronchodilator therapy with a multivitamin supplement.
